title: Layered config merge with deletes and list appends
requirements: merge(base, override) merges nested dicts recursively; lists and scalars in override replace base values
An override value of None deletes that key
Neither input is mutated and the result shares no mutable containers with them
(after the user switch) an override key '+name' appends its list to base['name'] instead of replacing it
user_messages: layered.merge(base, override) for our config files — nested dicts merge recursively, but lists and plain values from override just replace
None in the override means delete that key. and don't mutate either input, we reuse base for every environment
oh, one more: if an override key starts with '+', like '+plugins': ['x'], append to the base list instead of replacing it
